body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問：「訓練 loss 一直不跌。你第一個動作是加 layer、換更大 model，還是做 gradient check？」
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案：「我會加大 model，因為它可能不夠 capacity。」

## 先確認訓練訊號有沒有真的走到參數

一個 training loop 最少有 input、target、forward pass、loss、backward pass 和 optimiser update。任何一段接錯，較大的 model 只會更快消耗時間。常見問題包括 target encoding 與 loss function 不匹配、資料和 label 對錯行、忘了清 gradient、optimizer 沒有拿到正確 parameter、學習率尺度不合理、tensor shape 被 broadcast 後仍可運行，或者 evaluation mode 和 training mode 混在一起。先把資料縮到可手算、可觀察的一小批，才能分辨是模型不足，還是訊號根本沒有正確傳遞。

Gradient check 是一個很窄的診斷：對一個小模型和固定 input，微量改變某個參數，看看 loss 的數值差分方向和 backprop 算出的 gradient 是否大致一致。它不是每次正式訓練必須跑的東西，也不保證整個 pipeline 正確；它只是讓你在增加複雜度前，先檢查核心微分實作、loss 和 parameter connection 有沒有明顯斷線。另一個更實際的檢查是 overfit 一個極小 batch：如果系統連數個 synthetic examples 都學不到，先不要相信任何大規模 benchmark。

## 水未通，先查水管

你扭開水龍頭但花園沒有水，第一步不是買更長的水喉。先看水掣有沒有開、喉管有沒有接錯、哪裡漏水。Gradient check 像在一小段水管加壓，確認水確實可以流到盡頭。

## 答題時要交代嘅判斷

有系統地由最小 case 往上加：固定 seed、打印一個 batch 的 input/target、確認 output shape、記錄 loss、檢查 parameter update 大小，然後只改一個變數。若 tiny batch 能 overfit 而 validation 仍差，才看 data split、label quality、regularisation 或 capacity。這個次序展示你能分開 implementation bug、資料問題和 generalisation 問題，而不是把所有問題稱為「模型不夠大」。

## 答案何時會太薄

只看一條 loss curve 或把 learning rate 掃很大範圍都不足夠。先做最小 baseline，例如 linear model 或兩層 network，配一個人能檢查的 synthetic mapping。若 baseline 的輸入、目標、loss 和預期輸出都說不清楚，不應引入 transformer、distributed training 或複雜 scheduler。

## 技術證據

Portfolio 可以有 `tiny-overfit.ipynb` 或英文 source script、`gradient-check.md`、固定 seed 的 `fixtures.jsonl`、shape assertions、one-batch log、loss curve、parameter-before-after diff 和一組 deliberately broken tests。README 寫明 numerical tolerance、浮點誤差的限制、何時關閉 gradient check，以及如何重跑。把大型實驗輸出和 small proof 分開，讓 reviewer 可以在數分鐘內看到核心是否正常。

## 交付、業務與風險證據

用 `debug-decision-log.md` 寫明哪個 failure 阻止了下一階段、誰確認 tiny proof 足夠、何時不得進入更昂貴訓練，以及模型輸出在所有 check 前不會支持真實決定。這樣能展示你管理的是不確定性和成本，而不是把 GPU 時數或合成分數當成果。若要交接給別人，附上最小 rerun command、已知限制和停止條件。

## 延伸閱讀

[ML learning modes 與 baseline](/zh-HK/articles/ml-learning-modes-and-baselines)、[regularisation、loss 與 generalisation](/zh-HK/articles/regularisation-loss-and-generalisation) 和 [由模糊需求到可驗收 feature](/zh-HK/articles/from-vague-request-to-accepted-feature)。

## 範圍說明

這是 AI.DOG 的單題練習。訓練資料、log、數字、程式片段和 artefact 都是虛構或 synthetic 的教學草稿；不代表任何真實產品模型、公司系統或部署效果。

body.en:
> Interviewer asks: “Training loss will not fall. Is your first move to add layers, choose a larger model, or run a gradient check?”
>
> Half-right answer: “I would use a larger model because the current one may lack capacity.”

## Check that the training signal reaches the parameters

A training loop needs, at minimum, an input, target, forward pass, loss, backward pass, and optimiser update. If any connection is wrong, a larger model only burns time faster. Common failures include a target encoding that does not match the loss function, rows of data and labels out of alignment, uncleared gradients, an optimiser with the wrong parameters, an unsuitable learning-rate scale, a tensor shape that broadcasts while remaining wrong, or mixed training and evaluation modes. Shrink the system to a batch you can inspect and partly calculate before deciding that capacity is the problem.

A gradient check is a narrow diagnostic. On a small model and fixed input, nudge one parameter slightly and compare the numerical change in loss with the backpropagated gradient direction. It is not required on every production run and cannot prove the entire pipeline correct. It simply checks whether the core differentiation, loss, and parameter connection are obviously broken before complexity grows. A practical companion check is overfitting a tiny batch: if the system cannot learn a few synthetic examples, do not trust a large benchmark yet.

## Before a bigger model, check the pipe

You turn on a tap and the garden remains dry. Buying a longer hose is not the first step. Check the valve, the connections, and leaks. A gradient check is like pressurising a small section of hose to confirm water can reach the end.

## The judgement an interviewer is listening for

Move upward from a smallest case: fix the seed, print one batch of input and target, confirm output shape, record loss, inspect the parameter-update size, and change one variable at a time. If a tiny batch can overfit but validation remains poor, then investigate the split, label quality, regularisation, or capacity. This order separates an implementation bug, a data problem, and a generalisation problem instead of calling every failure “the model is too small.”

## Where an answer goes thin

One loss curve or a broad learning-rate sweep is not enough. Build a minimal baseline, such as a linear model or two-layer network, around a synthetic mapping a person can inspect. If the input, target, loss, and expected output of that baseline are unclear, do not add a transformer, distributed training, or a complex scheduler.

## Technical evidence

A portfolio can contain `tiny-overfit.ipynb` or an English source script, `gradient-check.md`, fixed-seed `fixtures.jsonl`, shape assertions, a one-batch log, loss curve, parameter-before-and-after diff, and deliberately broken tests. The README should state numerical tolerance, floating-point limits, when gradient checking is disabled, and how to rerun it. Keep large experiment output separate from the small proof so a reviewer can inspect the core quickly.

## Delivery, business, and risk evidence

Use `debug-decision-log.md` to state which failure blocks the next phase, who decides the tiny proof is sufficient, when expensive training must not start, and why no model output supports a real decision before these checks. That demonstrates management of uncertainty and cost, rather than presenting GPU time or synthetic scores as an achievement. For handoff, include the smallest rerun command, known limits, and stop conditions.

## Further reading

[ML learning modes and baselines](/en/articles/ml-learning-modes-and-baselines), [regularisation, loss, and generalisation](/en/articles/regularisation-loss-and-generalisation), and [turn a vague request into an accepted feature](/en/articles/from-vague-request-to-accepted-feature).

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG single-question practice exercise. Training data, logs, numbers, code fragments, and artefacts are fictional or synthetic teaching-draft material. They do not represent a real product model, company system, or deployment effect.
